dedupe_keys.name: national and regional water point inventories on hdx afghanistan south sudan uganda liberia sierra leone ethiopia

description: This record groups national and regional water point inventories published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange that are not country slices of WPdx: Afghanistan's water point coordinates and safe water coverage from the Ministry of Rural Rehabilitation and Development (2022, UNICEF as source), South Sudan's water points from the Water Information Management System of the Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation (2012), GPS water sources for northern Uganda compiled by OCHA from WASH partners (2009 to 2011), Liberia's national water point mapping and Sierra Leone's 2012 national mapping collected with Akvo Flow, a second copy of the Sierra Leone 2012 survey by MapAction (Ministry of Water Resources with the World Bank WSP, UNICEF and partners), a multi-source Ethiopian water point collection from mWater tagged by admin level (3iS, marked use with caution), and functionality of water schemes in Tigray (May 2024). The producers are the ministries and partners named; OCHA offices, Akvo, MapAction and 3iS published them. Coverage is national for five countries and regional for northern Uganda and Tigray. All are a free download from HDX as CSV, XLSX, shapefile or GeoPackage, under CC BY, CC BY-IGO or HDX's "Other" licence. Caveats: most are one-off surveys that are now old, schemas differ, and some overlap WPdx. Simulation uses: rural water supply inventories and functionality for capacity planning and drought resilience. Related record: the Water Point Data Exchange (data-wpdx-water-point-data-exchange).
licence: Mixed per dataset (CC BY, CC BY-IGO or HDX Other)

schema_summary: water point locations with type, installer and quality (Sierra Leone 2012), safe water coverage by point (Afghanistan), WIMS attributes (South Sudan), GPS water sources (northern Uganda), Akvo Flow survey fields (Liberia, Sierra Leone), mWater multi-source points with admin tags (Ethiopia), functionality of motorised and non-motorised schemes by zone and woreda (Tigray)
